isonocardicin synthase. S-adenosyl-L-methionine + nocardicin G = S-methyl-5'-thioadenosine + isonocardicin C
4-hydroxybenzoate polyprenyltransferase. all-trans-polyprenyl diphosphate + 4-hydroxybenzoate = 4-hydroxy-3-(all-trans-polyprenyl)benzoate + diphosphate

cysteine synthase. O-acetyl-L-serine + hydrogen sulfide = L-cysteine + acetate
cystathionine gamma-synthase. O4-succinyl-L-homoserine + L-cysteine = L-cystathionine + succinate
O-acetylhomoserine aminocarboxypropyltransferase. O-acetyl-L-homoserine + methanethiol = L-methionine + acetate
galactose-6-sulfurylase. Eliminates sulfate from the D-galactose 6-sulfate residues of porphyran, producing 3,6-anhydrogalactose residues
zeatin 9-aminocarboxyethyltransferase. O-acetyl-L-serine + zeatin = lupinate + acetate
beta-pyrazolylalanine synthase. O-acetyl-L-serine + pyrazole = 3-(pyrazol-1-yl)-L-alanine + acetate
L-mimosine synthase. O-acetyl-L-serine + 3,4-dihydroxypyridine = 3-(3,4-dihydroxypyridin-1-yl)-L-alanine + acetate
uracilylalanine synthase. O-acetyl-L-serine + uracil = 3-(uracil-1-yl)-L-alanine + acetate

2-succinyl-6-hydroxy-2,4-cyclohexadiene-1-carboxylate synthase. 2-oxoglutarate + isochorismate = (1R,6R)-6-hydroxy-2-succinylcyclohexa-2,4-diene-1-carboxylate + pyruvate + CO2

[protein ADP-ribosylarginine] hydrolase. (1) protein-Nomega-(ADP-D-ribosyl)-L-arginine + H2O = ADP-D-ribose + protein-L-arginine;;(2) Nomega-(ADP-D-ribosyl)-L-arginine + H2O = ADP-D-ribose + L-arginine
inosine nucleosidase. inosine + H2O = D-ribose + hypoxanthine
DNA-3-methyladenine glycosylase I. Hydrolysis of alkylated DNA, releasing 3-methyladenine
DNA-3-methyladenine glycosylase II. Hydrolysis of alkylated DNA, releasing 3-methyladenine, 3-methylguanine, 7-methylguanine and 7-methyladenine
rRNA N-glycosylase. Hydrolysis of the N-glycosylic bond at A-4324 in 28S rRNA from rat ribosomes
DNA-formamidopyrimidine glycosylase. Hydrolysis of DNA containing ring-opened 7-methylguanine residues, releasing 2,6-diamino-4-hydroxy-5-(N-methyl)formamidopyrimidine
ADP-ribosyl-[dinitrogen reductase] hydrolase. [dinitrogen reductase]-Nomega-alpha-(ADP-D-ribosyl)-L-arginine + H2O = ADP-D-ribose + [dinitrogen reductase]-L-arginine
N-methyl nucleosidase. 7-methylxanthosine + H2O = 7-methylxanthine + D-ribose
futalosine hydrolase. futalosine + H2O = dehypoxanthine futalosine + hypoxanthine
uracil-DNA glycosylase. Hydrolyses single-stranded DNA or mismatched double-stranded DNA and polynucleotides, releasing free uracil
double-stranded uracil-DNA glycosylase. Specifically hydrolyses mismatched double-stranded DNA and polynucleotides, releasing free uracil
thymine-DNA glycosylase. Hydrolyses mismatched double-stranded DNA and polynucleotides, releasing free thymine.
uridine nucleosidase. uridine + H2O = D-ribose + uracil
aminodeoxyfutalosine nucleosidase. 6-amino-6-deoxyfutalosine + H2O = dehypoxanthine futalosine + adenine
adenine glycosylase. Hydrolyses free adenine bases from 7,8-dihydro-8-oxoguanine:adenine mismatched double-stranded DNA, leaving an apurinic site.
AMP nucleosidase. AMP + H2O = D-ribose 5-phosphate + adenine
NAD+ glycohydrolase. NAD+ + H2O = ADP-D-ribose + nicotinamide
ADP-ribosyl cyclase/cyclic ADP-ribose hydrolase. NAD+ + H2O = ADP-D-ribose + nicotinamide (overall reaction);;(1a) NAD+ = cyclic ADP-ribose + nicotinamide;;(1b) cyclic ADP-ribose + H2O = ADP-D-ribose
adenosine nucleosidase. adenosine + H2O = D-ribose + adenine
ribosylpyrimidine nucleosidase. a pyrimidine nucleoside + H2O = D-ribose + a pyrimidine base

adenosylhomocysteine nucleosidase. (1) S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + H2O = S-(5-deoxy-D-ribos-5-yl)-L-homocysteine + adenine;;(2) 5'-deoxyadenosine + H2O = 5-deoxy-D-ribose + adenine;;(3) S-methyl-5'-thioadenosine + H2O = 5-(methylsulfanyl)-D-ribose + adenine
Hydrolysing S-glycosyl compounds (deleted sub-subclass)
Acting on ether bonds
Thioether and trialkylsulfonium hydrolases (deleted sub-subclass)
adenosylhomocysteinase. S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine + H2O = L-homocysteine + adenosine
S-adenosyl-L-methionine hydrolase (L-homoserine-forming). S-adenosyl-L-methionine + H2O = L-homoserine + S-methyl-5'-thioadenosine
Ether hydrolases
isochorismatase. isochorismate + H2O = (2S,3S)-2,3-dihydroxy-2,3-dihydrobenzoate + pyruvate
soluble epoxide hydrolase. an epoxide + H2O = a glycol

cholesterol-5,6-oxide hydrolase. (1) 5,6alpha-epoxy-5alpha-cholestan-3beta-ol + H2O = 5alpha-cholestane-3beta,5alpha,6beta-triol;;(2) 5,6beta-epoxy-5beta-cholestan-3beta-ol + H2O = 5alpha-cholestane-3beta,5alpha,6beta-triol
oxepin-CoA hydrolase. 2-oxepin-2(3H)-ylideneacetyl-CoA + H2O = 3-oxo-5,6-dehydrosuberyl-CoA semialdehyde
chorismatase. chorismate + H2O = (4R,5R)-4,5-dihydroxycyclohexa-1(6),2-diene-1-carboxylate + pyruvate
2,4-dinitroanisole O-demethylase. 2,4-dinitroanisole + H2O = methanol + 2,4-dinitrophenol
trans-2,3-dihydro-3-hydroxyanthranilic acid synthase. (2S)-2-amino-4-deoxychorismate + H2O = (5S,6S)-6-amino-5-hydroxycyclohexa-1,3-diene-1-carboxylate + pyruvate

lysoplasmalogenase. (1) 1-(1-alkenyl)-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine + H2O = an aldehyde + sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine;;(2) 1-(1-alkenyl)-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine + H2O = an aldehyde + sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine
epoxide hydrolase. an epoxide + H2O = a glycol
trans-epoxysuccinate hydrolase. trans-2,3-epoxysuccinate + H2O = meso-tartrate
alkenylglycerophosphoethanolamine hydrolase. 1-(1-alkenyl)-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine + H2O = an aldehyde + sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine
leukotriene-A4 hydrolase. leukotriene A4 + H2O = leukotriene B4
hepoxilin-epoxide hydrolase. hepoxilin A3 + H2O = trioxilin A3
limonene-1,2-epoxide hydrolase. 1,2-epoxymenth-8-ene + H2O = menth-8-ene-1,2-diol

microsomal epoxide hydrolase. (1) cis-stilbene oxide + H2O = (1R,2R)-1,2-diphenylethane-1,2-diol;;(2) 1-(4-methoxyphenyl)-N-methyl-N-[(3-methyloxetan-3-yl)methyl]methanamine + H2O = 2-({[(4-methoxyphenyl)methyl](methyl)amino}methyl)-2-methylpropane-1,3-diol
Acting on peptide bonds (peptidases)
α-Amino-acyl-peptide hydrolases (deleted sub-subclass)
Aminopeptidases

leucyl aminopeptidase. Release of an N-terminal amino acid, Xaa!Yaa-, in which Xaa is preferably Leu, but may be other amino acids including Pro although not Arg or Lys, and Yaa may be Pro. Amino acid amides and methyl esters are also readily hydrolysed, but rates on arylamides are exceedingly low
bacterial leucyl aminopeptidase. Release of an N-terminal amino acid, preferentially leucine, but not glutamic or aspartic acids
clostridial aminopeptidase. Release of any N-terminal amino acid, including proline and hydroxyproline, but no cleavage of Xaa-Pro-
cytosol alanyl aminopeptidase. Release of an N-terminal amino acid, preferentially alanine, from a wide range of peptides, amides and arylamides
aminopeptidase Y. Preferentially, release of N-terminal lysine

Xaa-Trp aminopeptidase. Release of a variety of N-terminal residues (especially glutamate and leucine) from peptides, provided tryptophan (or at least phenylalanine or tyrosine) is the penultimate residue. Also acts on Glu!Trp, Leu!Trp and a number of other dipeptides
tryptophanyl aminopeptidase. Preferential release of N-terminal tryptophan
methionyl aminopeptidase. Release of N-terminal amino acids, preferentially methionine, from peptides and arylamides

D-stereospecific aminopeptidase. Release of an N-terminal D-amino acid from a peptide, Xaa!Yaa-, in which Xaa is preferably D-Ala, D-Ser or D-Thr. D-Amino acid amides and methyl esters also are hydrolysed, as is glycine amide

membrane alanyl aminopeptidase. Release of an N-terminal amino acid, Xaa!Yaa- from a peptide, amide or arylamide. Xaa is preferably Ala, but may be most amino acids including Pro (slow action). When a terminal hydrophobic residue is followed by a prolyl residue, the two may be released as an intact Xaa-Pro dipeptide

aminopeptidase Ey. Differs from other aminopeptidases in broad specificity for amino acids in the P1 position and the ability to hydrolyse peptides of four or five residues that contain Pro in the P1' position
aspartyl aminopeptidase. Release of an N-terminal aspartate or glutamate from a peptide, with a preference for aspartate
aminopeptidase I. Release of an N-terminal amino acid, preferably a neutral or hydrophobic one, from a polypeptide. Aminoacyl-arylamides are poor substrates
PepB aminopeptidase. Release of an N-terminal amino acid, Xaa, from a peptide or arylamide. Xaa is preferably Glu or Asp but may be other amino acids, including Leu, Met, His, Cys and Gln
aminopeptidase S. Release of an N-terminal amino acid with a preference for large hydrophobic amino-terminus residues
beta-peptidyl aminopeptidase. Cleaves N-terminal beta-homoamino acids from peptides composed of 2 to 6 amino acids

intermediate cleaving peptidase 55. The enzyme cleaves the Pro36-Pro37 bond of cysteine desulfurase (EC 2.8.1.7) removing three amino acid residues (Tyr-Ser-Pro) from the N-terminus after cleavage by mitochondrial processing peptidase.

archaeal arginyl aminopeptidase. Release of an N-terminal L-arginine from a protein with only minimal activity against other amino acids. L-Arg-7-amido-4-methylcoumarin is the best artificial substrate.

cystinyl aminopeptidase. Release of an N-terminal amino acid, Cys!Xaa-, in which the half-cystine residue is involved in a disulfide loop, notably in oxytocin or vasopressin. Hydrolysis rates on a range of aminoacyl arylamides exceed that for the cystinyl derivative, however [4]
tripeptide aminopeptidase. Release of the N-terminal residue from a tripeptide
prolyl aminopeptidase. Release of N-terminal proline from a peptide
aminopeptidase B. Release of N-terminal Arg and Lys from oligopeptides when P1' is not Pro. Also acts on arylamides of Arg and Lys
glutamyl aminopeptidase. Release of N-terminal glutamate (and to a lesser extent aspartate) from a peptide
Xaa-Pro aminopeptidase. Release of any N-terminal amino acid, including proline, that is linked to proline, even from a dipeptide or tripeptide
Peptidylamino-acid hydrolases or acylamino-acid hydrolases (deleted sub-subclass)
Dipeptidases
Met-Xaa dipeptidase. Hydrolysis of Met!Xaa dipeptides
non-stereospecific dipeptidase. Hydrolysis of dipeptides containing either D- or L-amino acids or both
cytosol nonspecific dipeptidase. Hydrolysis of dipeptides, preferentially hydrophobic dipeptides including prolyl amino acids
membrane dipeptidase. Hydrolysis of dipeptides
beta-Ala-His dipeptidase. Preferential hydrolysis of the beta-Ala!His dipeptide (carnosine), and also anserine, Xaa!His dipeptides and other dipeptides including homocarnosine
dipeptidase E. Dipeptidase E catalyses the hydrolysis of dipeptides Asp!Xaa. It does not act on peptides with N-terminal Glu, Asn or Gln, nor does it cleave isoaspartyl peptides
D-Ala-D-Ala dipeptidase. D-Ala-D-Ala + H2O = 2 D-Ala
cysteinylglycine-S-conjugate dipeptidase. an [L-cysteinylglycine]-S-conjugate + H2O = an L-cysteine-S-conjugate + glycine
Xaa-His dipeptidase. Hydrolysis of Xaa!His dipeptides
Xaa-Arg dipeptidase. Preferential hydrolysis of Xaa!Arg, Xaa!Lys or Xaa!ornithine dipeptides
Xaa-methyl-His dipeptidase. Hydrolysis of anserine (beta-alanyl!Npi-methyl-L-histidine), carnosine, homocarnosine, glycyl!leucine and other dipeptides with broad specificity
Glu-Glu dipeptidase. Hydrolysis of the Glu!Glu dipeptide
Xaa-Pro dipeptidase. Hydrolysis of Xaa!Pro dipeptides; also acts on aminoacyl-hydroxyproline analogs. No action on Pro-Pro
Dipeptidyl-peptidases and tripeptidyl-peptidases
dipeptidyl-peptidase I. Release of an N-terminal dipeptide, Xaa-Yaa!Zaa-, except when Xaa is Arg or Lys, or Yaa or Zaa is Pro
tripeptidyl-peptidase II. Release of an N-terminal tripeptide from a polypeptide
Xaa-Pro dipeptidyl-peptidase. Hydrolyses Xaa-Pro! bonds to release unblocked, N-terminal dipeptides from substrates including Ala-Pro!p-nitroanilide and (sequentially) Tyr-Pro!Phe-Pro!Gly-Pro!Ile
Xaa-Xaa-Pro tripeptidyl-peptidase. Hydrolysis of Xaa-Xaa-Pro!Yaa- releasing the N-terminal tripeptide of a peptide with Pro as the third residue (position P1) and where Yaa is not proline
gamma-D-glutamyl-L-lysine dipeptidyl-peptidase. The enzyme releases L-Ala-gamma-D-Glu dipeptides from cell wall peptides via cleavage of an L-Ala-gamma-D-Glu!L-Lys bond.

[mycofactocin precursor peptide] peptidase. C-terminal [mycofactocin precursor peptide]-glycyl-3-amino-5-[(4-hydroxyphenyl)methyl]-4,4-dimethylpyrrolidin-2-one + H2O = C-terminal [mycofactocin precursor peptide]-glycine + 3-amino-5-[(4-hydroxyphenyl)methyl]-4,4-dimethylpyrrolidin-2-one
dipeptidyl-peptidase II. Release of an N-terminal dipeptide, Xaa-Yaa!, preferentially when Yaa is Ala or Pro. Substrates are oligopeptides, preferentially tripeptides
dipeptidyl-peptidase III. Release of an N-terminal dipeptide from a peptide comprising four or more residues, with broad specificity. Also acts on dipeptidyl 2-naphthylamides.
dipeptidyl-peptidase IV. Release of an N-terminal dipeptide, Xaa-Yaa!Zaa-, from a polypeptide, preferentially when Yaa is Pro, provided Zaa is neither Pro nor hydroxyproline
dipeptidyl-dipeptidase. Preferential release of dipeptides from a tetrapeptide, e.g. Ala-Gly!Ala-Gly. Acts more slowly on Ala-Ala!Ala-Ala and Gly-Gly!Gly-Gly
tripeptidyl-peptidase I. Release of an N-terminal tripeptide from a polypeptide, but also has endopeptidase activity.
Peptidyl-dipeptidases

peptidyl-dipeptidase A. Release of a C-terminal dipeptide, oligopeptide!Xaa-Yaa, when Xaa is not Pro, and Yaa is neither Asp nor Glu. Thus, conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, with increase in vasoconstrictor activity, but no action on angiotensin II
peptidyl-dipeptidase B. Release of a C-terminal dipeptide or exceptionally a tripeptide
peptidyl-dipeptidase Dcp. Hydrolysis of unblocked, C-terminal dipeptides from oligopeptides, with broad specificity. Does not hydrolyse bonds in which P1' is Pro, or both P1 and P1' are Gly
cyanophycinase. [L-Asp(4-L-Arg)]n + H2O = [L-Asp(4-L-Arg)]n-1 + L-Asp(4-L-Arg)
Serine-type carboxypeptidases
lysosomal Pro-Xaa carboxypeptidase. Cleavage of a -Pro!Xaa bond to release a C-terminal amino acid
serine-type D-Ala-D-Ala carboxypeptidase. Preferential cleavage: (Ac)2-L-Lys-D-Ala!D-Ala. Also transpeptidation of peptidyl-alanyl moieties that are N-acyl substituents of D-alanine
carboxypeptidase C. Release of a C-terminal amino acid with broad specificity
carboxypeptidase D. Preferential release of a C-terminal arginine or lysine residue
Metallocarboxypeptidases
carboxypeptidase A. Release of a C-terminal amino acid, but little or no action with -Asp, -Glu, -Arg, -Lys or -Pro
carboxypeptidase E. Release of C-terminal arginine or lysine residues from polypeptides
glutamate carboxypeptidase. Release of C-terminal glutamate residues from a wide range of N-acylating moieties, including peptidyl, aminoacyl, benzoyl, benzyloxycarbonyl, folyl and pteroyl groups
carboxypeptidase M. Cleavage of C-terminal arginine or lysine residues from polypeptides
muramoyltetrapeptide carboxypeptidase. Hydrolysis of the bond: N-acetyl-D-glucosaminyl-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-Ala-D-glutamyl-meso-2,6-diaminoheptadioyl!D-alanine
zinc D-Ala-D-Ala carboxypeptidase. Cleavage of the bond: (Ac)2-L-lysyl-D-alanyl!D-alanine
carboxypeptidase A2. Similar to that of carboxypeptidase A (EC 3.4.17.1), but with a preference for bulkier C-terminal residues
membrane Pro-Xaa carboxypeptidase. Release of a C-terminal residue other than proline, by preferential cleavage of a prolyl bond
tubulinyl-Tyr carboxypeptidase. Cleavage of the -Glu!Tyr bond to release the C-terminal tyrosine residue from the native tyrosinated tubulin. Inactive on Z-Glu-Tyr
carboxypeptidase T. Releases a C-terminal residue, which may be hydrophobic or positively charged
carboxypeptidase Taq. Release of a C-terminal amino acid with broad specificity, except for -Pro
carboxypeptidase B. Preferential release of a C-terminal lysine or arginine amino acid
carboxypeptidase U. Release of C-terminal Arg and Lys from a polypeptide
glutamate carboxypeptidase II. Release of an unsubstituted, C-terminal glutamyl residue, typically from Ac-Asp-Glu or folylpoly-gamma-glutamates
metallocarboxypeptidase D. Releases C-terminal Arg and Lys from polypeptides
angiotensin-converting enzyme 2. angiotensin II + H2O = angiotensin-(1--7) + L-phenylalanine

tubulin-glutamate carboxypeptidase. This is a subfamily of enzymes that cleave C-terminal and/or side chain amino acids from tubulins. The dual-specificity enzymes can cleave both alpha- and gamma-linked L-glutamate from tubulins, removing the posttranslationally added polyglutamyl side chains from the C-terminal regions. In addition, the enzyme removes two glutamate residues from the C-terminus of beta-tubulin and detyrosinated alpha-tubulin (from which the C-terminal L-tyrosine has been removed by EC 3.4.17.17, tubulinyl-Tyr carboxypeptidase). The latter is cleaved to delta2-tubulin and further to delta3-tubulin.
glutathione-S-conjugate glycine hydrolase. a glutathione-S-conjugate + H2O = a [gamma-glutamyl-L-cysteine]-S-conjugate + glycine
lysine carboxypeptidase. Release of a C-terminal basic amino acid, preferentially lysine
Gly-Xaa carboxypeptidase. Release of a C-terminal amino acid from a peptide in which glycine is the penultimate amino acid, e.g. Z-Gly!Leu
alanine carboxypeptidase. Release of a C-terminal alanine from a peptide or a variety of pteroyl or acyl groups
muramoylpentapeptide carboxypeptidase. Cleavage of the bond UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanyl-gamma-D-glutamyl-meso-2,6-diaminoheptanedioyl-D-alanyl!D-alanine
Cysteine-type carboxypeptidases
cathepsin X. Release of C-terminal amino acid residues with broad specificity, but lacks action on C-terminal proline. Shows weak endopeptidase activity
Omega peptidases
acylaminoacyl-peptidase. (1) cleavage of an N-acetyl or N-formyl amino acid from the N-terminus of a polypeptide;;(2) internal cleavage of oxidized and glycated proteins

gamma-D-glutamyl-meso-diaminopimelate peptidase. Hydrolysis of gamma-D-glutamyl bonds to the L-terminus (position 7) of meso-diaminopimelic acid (meso-A2pm) in 7-(L-Ala-gamma-D-Glu)-meso-A2pm and 7-(L-Ala-gamma-D-Glu)-7-(D-Ala)-meso-A2pm. It is required that the D-terminal amino and carboxy groups of meso-A2pm are unsubstituted

ubiquitinyl hydrolase 1. Thiol-dependent hydrolysis of ester, thioester, amide, peptide and isopeptide bonds formed by the C-terminal Gly of ubiquitin (a 76-residue protein attached to proteins as an intracellular targeting signal)
glutathione gamma-glutamate hydrolase. (1) glutathione + H2O = L-cysteinylglycine + L-glutamate;;(2) a glutathione-S-conjugate + H2O = an (L-cysteinylglycine)-S-conjugate + L-glutamate
leukotriene-C4 hydrolase. leukotriene C4 + H2O = leukotriene D4 + L-glutamate
desampylase. an N6-[small archaeal modifier protein]-[protein]-L-lysine + H2O = a [protein]-L-lysine + a small archaeal modifier protein

glucosinolate gamma-glutamyl hydrolase. (1) an (E)-1-(glutathion-S-yl)-N-hydroxy-omega-(methylsulfanyl)alkan-1-imine + H2O = an (E)-1-(L-cysteinylglycin-S-yl)-N-hydroxy-omega-(methylsulfanyl)alkan-1-imine + L-glutamate;;(2) (E)-1-(glutathion-S-yl)-N-hydroxy-2-(1H-indol-3-yl)ethan-1-imine + H2O = (E)-1-(L-cysteinylglycin-S-yl)-N-hydroxy-2-(1H-indol-3-yl)ethan-1-imine + L-glutamate;;(3) (glutathion-S-yl)(1H-indol-3-yl)acetonitrile + H2O = (L-cysteinylglycin-S-yl)(1H-indol-3-yl)acetonitrile + L-glutamate;;(4) (Z)-1-(glutathion-S-yl)-N-hydroxy-2-phenylethan-1-imine + H2O = (Z)-1-(L-cysteinyglycin-S-yl)-N-hydroxy-2-phenylethan-1-imine + L-glutamate
peptidyl-glycinamidase. Cleavage of C-terminal glycinamide from polypeptides
pyroglutamyl-peptidase I. Release of an N-terminal pyroglutamyl group from a polypeptide, the second amino acid generally not being Pro
beta-aspartyl-peptidase. Cleavage of a beta-linked Asp residue from the N-terminus of a polypeptide
pyroglutamyl-peptidase II. Release of the N-terminal pyroglutamyl group from pGlu!His-Xaa tripeptides and pGlu!His-Xaa-Gly tetrapeptides
N-formylmethionyl-peptidase. Release of an N-terminal, formyl-methionyl residue from a polypeptide
folate gamma-glutamyl hydrolase. tetrahydropteroyl-(gamma-glutamyl)n + (n-1) H2O = 5,6,7,8-tetrahydrofolate + (n-1) L-glutamate
Peptidyl-amino-acid hydrolases (deleted sub-subclass)
Serine endopeptidases
chymotrypsin. Preferential cleavage: Tyr!, Trp!, Phe!, Leu!
acrosin. Preferential cleavage: Arg!, Lys!
sedolisin. Hydrolysis of the B chain of insulin at -Glu13!Ala-, -Leu15!Tyr- and -Phe25!Tyr-, and angiotensin I at -Tyr4!Ile-. A good synthetic substrate is Lys-Pro-Ile-Glu-Phe!Phe(NO2)-Arg-Leu.
xanthomonalisin. Cleavage of casein

C-terminal processing peptidase. The enzyme shows specific recognition of a C-terminal tripeptide, Xaa-Yaa-Zaa, in which Xaa is preferably Ala or Leu, Yaa is preferably Ala or Tyr, and Zaa is preferably Ala, but then cleaves at a variable distance from the C-terminus. A typical cleavage is -Ala-Ala!Arg-Ala-Ala-Lys-Glu-Asn-Tyr-Ala-Leu-Ala-Ala. In the plant chloroplast, the enzyme removes the C-terminal extension of the D1 polypeptide of photosystem II
physarolisin. Milk clotting activity. Preferential cleavage of Gly8!Ser in B chain of insulin most rapidly, followed by Leu11!Val, Cys(SO3H)19!Gly and Phe24!Phe. No action on Ac-Phe-Tyr(I)2.

mannan-binding lectin-associated serine protease-2. Selective cleavage after Arg223 in complement component C2 (-Ser-Leu-Gly-Arg!Lys-Ile-Gln-Ile) and after Arg76 in complement component C4 (-Gly-Leu-Gln-Arg!Ala-Leu-Glu-Ile)
rhomboid protease. Cleaves type-1 transmembrane domains using a catalytic dyad composed of serine and histidine that are contributed by different transmembrane domains
hepsin. Cleavage after basic amino-acid residues, with Arg strongly preferred to Lys
peptidase Do. Acts on substrates that are at least partially unfolded. The cleavage site P1 residue is normally between a pair of hydrophobic residues, such as Val!Val

HtrA2 peptidase. Cleavage of non-polar aliphatic amino-acids at the P1 position, with a preference for Val, Ile and Met. At the P2 and P3 positions, Arg is selected most strongly with a secondary preference for other hydrophilic residues
matriptase. Cleaves various synthetic substrates with Arg or Lys at the P1 position and prefers small side-chain amino acids, such as Ala and Gly, at the P2 position
C5a peptidase. The primary cleavage site is at His67!Lys68 in human C5a with a minor secondary cleavage site at Ala58!Ser59
aqualysin 1. Exhibits low specificity towards esters of amino acids with small hydrophobic or aromatic residues at the P1 position
site-1 protease. Processes precursors containing basic and hydrophobic/aliphatic residues at P4 and P2, respectively, with a relatively relaxed acceptance of amino acids at P1 and P3

pestivirus NS3 polyprotein peptidase. Leu is conserved at position P1 for all four cleavage sites. Alanine is found at position P1' of the NS4A-NS4B cleavage site, whereas serine is found at position P1' of the NS3-NS4A, NS4B-NS5A and NS5A-NS5B cleavage sites
equine arterivirus serine peptidase. Cleavage of (Glu/Gln)!(Gly/Ser/Ala) in arterivirus replicase translation products ORF1a and ORF1ab

infectious pancreatic necrosis birnavirus Vp4 peptidase. Cleaves the (Ser/Thr)-Xaa-Ala!(Ser/Ala)-Gly motif in the polyprotein NH2-pVP2-VP4-VP3-COOH of infectious pancreatic necrosis virus at the pVP2-VP4 and VP4-VP3 junctions
SpoIVB peptidase. Self-cleaves Val52!Asn53, Ala62!Phe63 and Val74!Thr75 at the N-terminus of SpoIVB
stratum corneum chymotryptic enzyme. Cleavage of proteins with aromatic side chains in the P1 position
kallikrein 8. Cleavage of amide substrates following the basic amino acids Arg or Lys at the P1 position, with a preference for Arg over Lys

kallikrein 13. Hydrolyses mouse Ren2 protein (a species of prorenin present in the submandibular gland) on the carboxy side of the arginine residue at the Lys-Arg! pair in the N-terminus, to yield mature renin
alpha-lytic endopeptidase. Preferential cleavage: Ala!, Val! in bacterial cell walls, elastin and other proteins
oviductin. Preferential cleavage at Gly-Ser-Arg373! of glycoprotein gp43 in Xenopus laevis coelemic egg envelope to yield gp41
Lys-Lys/Arg-Xaa endopeptidase. Cleavage of -Lys-Lys! and -Lys-Arg! bonds.
transmembrane protease serine 2. The enzyme cleaves angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (EC 3.4.17.23) and cleaves influenzea A and B virus and coronavirus spike glycoproteins at arginine residues.

kumamolysin. The enzyme preferentially hydrolyses peptides having an Ala or Pro residue at P2 position and prefers such charged amino acid residues as Glu or Arg at the P2' position. In the oxidized insulin B chain, kumamolysin preferentially cleaves between Leu15 and Tyr16
glutamyl endopeptidase. Preferential cleavage: Glu!, Asp!
chymotrypsin C. Preferential cleavage: Leu!, Tyr!, Phe!, Met!, Trp!, Gln!, Asn!
cathepsin G. Specificity similar to chymotrypsin C
coagulation factor VIIa. Selective cleavage of Arg!Ile bond in factor X to form factor Xa
coagulation factor IXa. Selective cleavage of Arg!Ile bond in factor X to form factor Xa
cucumisin. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity
prolyl oligopeptidase. Hydrolysis of ---Pro! and to a lesser extent ---Ala! in oligopeptides
coagulation factor XIa. Selective cleavage of Arg!Ala and Arg!Val bonds in factor IX to form factor IXa
metridin. Preferential cleavage: Tyr!, Phe!, Leu!; little action on Trp-!

brachyurin. Hydrolysis of proteins, with broad specificity for peptide bonds. Native collagen is cleaved about 75% of the length of the molecule from the N-terminus. Low activity on small molecule substrates of both trypsin and chymotrypsin
plasma kallikrein. Selective cleavage of some Arg! and Lys! bonds, including Lys!Arg and Arg!Ser in (human) kininogen to release bradykinin

tissue kallikrein. Preferential cleavage of Arg! bonds in small molecule substrates. Highly selective action to release kallidin (lysyl-bradykinin) from kininogen involves hydrolysis of Met! or Leu!. The rat enzyme is unusual in liberating bradykinin directly from autologous kininogens by cleavage at two Arg! bonds [5]
pancreatic elastase. Hydrolysis of proteins, including elastin. Preferential cleavage: Ala!
leukocyte elastase. Hydrolysis of proteins, including elastin. Preferential cleavage Val! > Ala!
coagulation factor XIIa. Selective cleavage of Arg!Ile bonds in factor VII to form factor VIIa and factor XI to form factor XIa
chymase. Preferential cleavage: Phe! > Tyr! > Trp! > Leu!
trypsin. Preferential cleavage: Arg!, Lys!
complement subcomponent C_overbar_1r_. Selective cleavage of Lys(or Arg)!Ile bond in complement subcomponent C1s to form C_overbar_1s_ (EC 3.4.21.42)

complement subcomponent C_overbar_1s_. Cleavage of Arg!Ala bond in complement component C4 to form C4a and C4b, and Lys(or Arg)!Lys bond in complement component C2 to form C2a and C2b: the "classical" pathway C3 convertase

classical-complement-pathway C3/C5 convertase. Selective cleavage of Arg!Ser bond in complement component C3 alpha-chain to form C3a and C3b, and Arg! bond in complement component C5 alpha-chain to form C5a and C5b
complement factor I. Inactivates complement subcomponents C3b, iC3b and C4b by proteolytic cleavage
complement factor D. Selective cleavage of Arg!Lys bond in complement factor B when in complex with complement subcomponent C3b or with cobra venom factor

alternative-complement-pathway C3/C5 convertase. Cleavage of Arg!Ser bond in complement component C3 alpha-chain to yield C3a and C3b, and Arg! bond in complement component C5 alpha-chain to yield C5a and C5b
cerevisin. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity, and of Bz-Arg-OEt Ac-Tyr-OEt. Does not hydrolyse peptide amides
hypodermin C. Hydrolysis of proteins including native collagen at !Ala bond leaving an N-terminal (75%) and a C-terminal (25%) fragment
thrombin. Selective cleavage of Arg!Gly bonds in fibrinogen to form fibrin and release fibrinopeptides A and B
lysyl endopeptidase. Preferential cleavage: Lys!, including -Lys!Pro-
endopeptidase La. Hydrolysis of proteins in presence of ATP

gamma-renin. Cleavage of the Leu!Leu bond in synthetic tetradecapeptide renin substrate (horse), to produce angiotensin I, but not active on natural angiotensinogen, unlike renin (EC 3.4.23.15). Also hydrolyses Bz-Arg-p-nitroanilide
venombin AB. Selective cleavage at Arg! bonds in fibrinogen to form fibrin and release fibrinopeptides A and B
leucyl endopeptidase. Hydrolysis of proteins. Preferential cleavage: Leu! in small molecule substrates
tryptase. Preferential cleavage: Arg!, Lys!, but with more restricted specificity than trypsin
coagulation factor Xa. Selective cleavage of Arg!Thr and then Arg!Ile bonds in prothrombin to form thrombin
scutelarin. Selective cleavage of Arg!Thr and Arg!Ile in prothrombin to form thrombin and two inactive fragments
kexin. Cleavage of -Lys-Arg! and -Arg-Arg! bonds to process yeast alpha-factor pheromone and killer toxin precursors
subtilisin. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds, and a preference for a large uncharged residue in P1. Hydrolyses peptide amides
oryzin. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity, and of Bz-Arg-OEt > Ac-Tyr-OEt. Does not hydrolyse peptide amides
peptidase K. Hydrolysis of keratin, and of other proteins with subtilisin-like specificity. Hydrolyses peptide amides
thermomycolin. Rather nonspecific hydrolysis of proteins. Preferential cleavage: Ala!, Tyr!, Phe! in small molecule substrates
thermitase. Hydrolysis of proteins, including collagen
endopeptidase So. Hydrolysis of proteins, but not Bz-Tyr-OEt, Ac-Phe-beta-naphthylester, or Bz-Arg-OEt
t-plasminogen activator. Specific cleavage of Arg!Val bond in plasminogen to form plasmin
activated protein C (thrombin-activated peptidase). Degradation of blood coagulation factors Va and VIIIa
plasmin. Preferential cleavage: Lys! > Arg!; higher selectivity than trypsin. Converts fibrin into soluble products
pancreatic endopeptidase E. Preferential cleavage: Ala!. Does not hydrolyse elastin
pancreatic elastase II. Preferential cleavage: Leu!, Met! and Phe!. Hydrolyses elastin
IgA-specific serine endopeptidase. Cleavage of immunoglobulin A molecules at certain Pro! bonds in the hinge region. No small molecule substrates are known
u-plasminogen activator. Specific cleavage of Arg!Val bond in plasminogen to form plasmin
venombin A. Selective cleavage of Arg! bond in fibrinogen, to form fibrin, and release fibrinopeptide A. The specificity of further degradation of fibrinogen varies with species origin of the enzyme

furin. Release of mature proteins from their proproteins by cleavage of -Arg-Xaa-Yaa-Arg! bonds, where Xaa can by any amino acid and Yaa is Arg or Lys. Releases albumin, complement component C3 and von Willebrand factor from their respective precursors
myeloblastin. Hydrolysis of proteins, including elastin, by preferential cleavage: -Ala! > -Val!
semenogelase. Preferential cleavage: -Tyr!
granzyme A. Hydrolysis of proteins, including fibronectin, type IV collagen and nucleolin. Preferential cleavage: -Arg!, -Lys! >> -Phe! in small molecule substrates
granzyme B. Preferential cleavage: -Asp! >> -Asn! > -Met!, -Ser!
streptogrisin A. Hydrolysis of proteins with specificity similar to chymotrypsin
streptogrisin B. Hydrolysis of proteins with trypsin-like specificity
glutamyl endopeptidase II. Preferential cleavage: -Glu! >> -Asp! . Preference for Pro or Leu at P2 and Phe at P3. Cleavage of -Glu!Asp- and -Glu!Pro- bonds is slow
oligopeptidase B. Hydrolysis of -Arg!, -Lys! bonds in oligopeptides, even when P1' residue is proline

limulus clotting factor _overbar_C_. Selective cleavage of -Arg103!Ser- and -Ile124!Ile- bonds in limulus clotting factor B to form factor _overbar_B_. Cleavage of -Pro-Arg! bonds in synthetic substrates
limulus clotting factor _overbar_B_. Selective cleavage of -Arg98!Ile- bond in limulus proclotting enzyme to form active clotting enzyme
limulus clotting enzyme. Selective cleavage of -Arg18! and -Arg47! bonds in coagulogen to form coagulin and fragments
omptin. Preferential cleavage: -Xaa!Yaa- in which both Xaa and Yaa are Lys or Arg
repressor LexA. Hydrolysis of Ala84!Gly bond in repressor LexA
signal peptidase I. Cleavage of hydrophobic, N-terminal signal or leader sequences
enteropeptidase. Activation of trypsinogen by selective cleavage of Lys6!Ile bond
togavirin. Autocatalytic release of the core protein from the N-terminus of the togavirus structural polyprotein by hydrolysis of a -Trp!Ser- bond
flavivirin. Selective hydrolysis of -Xaa-Xaa!Yaa- bonds in which each of the Xaa can be either Arg or Lys and Yaa can be either Ser or Ala

endopeptidase Clp. Hydrolysis of proteins to small peptides in the presence of ATP and Mg2+. alpha-Casein is the usual test substrate. In the absence of ATP, only oligopeptides shorter than five residues are hydrolysed (such as succinyl-Leu-Tyr!NHMec; and Leu-Tyr-Leu!Tyr-Trp, in which cleavage of the -Tyr!Leu- and -Tyr!Trp bonds also occurs)
proprotein convertase 1. Release of protein hormones, neuropeptides and renin from their precursors, generally by hydrolysis of -Lys-Arg! bonds
proprotein convertase 2. Release of protein hormones and neuropeptides from their precursors, generally by hydrolysis of -Lys-Arg! bonds

snake venom factor V activator. Fully activates human clotting factor V by a single cleavage at the Trp-Tyr-Leu-Arg1545!Ser-Asn-Asn-Gly bond. Cattle, but not rabbit, factor V is cleaved, and no other proteins of the clotting system are attacked. Esterase activity is observed on Bz-Arg-OEt and Tos-Arg-OMe, and amidase activity on Phe-pipecolyl-Arg-NHPhNO2

lactocepin. Endopeptidase activity with very broad specificity, although some subsite preferences have been noted, e.g. large hydrophobic residues in the P1 and P4 positions, and Pro in the P2 position [1,2]. Best known for its action on caseins, although it has been shown to hydrolyse hemoglobin and oxidized insulin B chain
assemblin. Cleaves -Ala!Ser- and -Ala!Ala- bonds in the scaffold protein
hepacivirin. Hydrolysis of four peptide bonds in the viral precursor polyprotein, commonly with Asp or Glu in the P6 position, Cys or Thr in P1 and Ser or Ala in P1'
spermosin. Hydrolyses arginyl bonds, preferably with Pro in the P2 position
Cysteine endopeptidases

cathepsin B. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds. Preferentially cleaves -Arg-Arg! bonds in small molecule substrates (thus differing from cathepsin L). In addition to being an endopeptidase, shows peptidyl-dipeptidase activity, liberating C-terminal dipeptides
streptopain. Preferential cleavage with hydrophobic residues at P2, P1 and P1'
actinidain. Similar to that of papain

cathepsin L. Similar to that of papain. As compared to cathepsin B, cathepsin L exhibits higher activity towards protein substrates, but has little activity on Z-Arg-Arg-NHMec, and no peptidyl-dipeptidase activity
cathepsin H. Hydrolysis of proteins, acting as an aminopeptidase (notably, cleaving Arg! bonds) as well as an endopeptidase
papain. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds, but preference for an amino acid bearing a large hydrophobic side chain at the P2 position. Does not accept Val in P1'
cathepsin T. Interconversion of the three forms of tyrosine aminotransferase, EC 2.6.1.5
glycyl endopeptidase. Preferential cleavage: Gly!, in proteins and small molecule substrates
cancer procoagulant. Specific cleavage of Arg!Ile bond in Factor X to form Factor Xa
cathepsin S. Similar to cathepsin L, but with much less activity on Z-Phe-Arg!NHMec, and more activity on the Z-Val-Val-Arg! compound
picornain 3C. Selective cleavage of Gln!Gly bond in the poliovirus polyprotein. In other picornavirus reactions Glu may be substituted for Gln, and Ser or Thr for Gly
picornain 2A. Selective cleavage of Tyr!Gly bond in picornavirus polyprotein
ficain. Similar to that of papain
caricain. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds, similar to those of papain and chymopapain
ananain. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds. Best reported small molecule substrate Bz-Phe-Val-Arg!NHMec, but broader specificity than fruit bromelain
stem bromelain. Broad specificity for cleavage of proteins, but strong preference for Z-Arg-Arg!NHMec amongst small molecule substrates
fruit bromelain. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds. Bz-Phe-Val-Arg!NHMec is a good synthetic substrate, but there is no action on Z-Arg-Arg-NHMec (c.f. stem bromelain)
legumain. Hydrolysis of proteins and small molecule substrates at -Asn!Xaa- bonds
histolysain. Hydrolysis of proteins, including basement membrane collagen and azocasein. Preferential cleavage: Arg-Arg! in small molecule substrates including Z-Arg-Arg!NHMec
caspase-1. Strict requirement for an Asp residue at position P1 and has a preferred cleavage sequence of Tyr-Val-Ala-Asp!
gingipain R. Hydrolysis of proteins and small molecule substrates, with a preference for Arg in P1
cathepsin K. Broad proteolytic activity. With small-molecule substrates and inhibitors, the major determinant of specificity is P2, which is preferably Leu, Met Phe, and not Arg
adenain. Cleaves proteins of the adenovirus and its host cell at two consensus sites: -Yaa-Xaa-Gly-Gly!Xaa- and -Yaa-Xaa-Gly-Xaa!Gly- (in which Yaa is Met, Ile or Leu, and Xaa is any amino acid)

bleomycin hydrolase. Inactivates bleomycin B2 (a cytotoxic glycometallopeptide) by hydrolysis of a carboxyamide bond of beta-aminoalanine, but also shows general aminopeptidase activity. The specificity varies somewhat with source, but amino acid arylamides of Met, Leu and Ala are preferred [1]
cathepsin F. The recombinant enzyme cleaves synthetic substrates with Phe and Leu (better than Val) in P2, with high specificity constant (kcat/Km) comparable to that of cathepsin L
cathepsin O. The recombinant human enzyme hydrolyses synthetic endopeptidase substrates including Z-Phe-Arg-NHMec and Z-Arg-Arg-NHMec
cathepsin V. The recombinant enzyme hydrolyses proteins (serum albumin, collagen) and synthetic substrates (Z-Phe-Arg-NHMec > Z-Leu-Arg-NHMec > Z-Val-Arg-NHMec)

nuclear-inclusion-a endopeptidase. Hydrolyses glutaminyl bonds, and activity is further restricted by preferences for the amino acids in P6 - P1' that vary with the species of potyvirus, e.g. Glu-Xaa-Xaa-Tyr-Xaa-Gln!(Ser or Gly) for the enzyme from tobacco etch virus. The natural substrate is the viral polyprotein, but other proteins and oligopeptides containing the appropriate consensus sequence are also cleaved.
helper-component proteinase. Hydrolyses a Gly!Gly bond at its own C-terminus, commonly in the sequence -Tyr-Xaa-Val-Gly!Gly, in the processing of the potyviral polyprotein

L-peptidase. Autocatalytically cleaves itself from the polyprotein of the foot-and-mouth disease virus by hydrolysis of a Lys!Gly bond, but then cleaves host cell initiation factor eIF-4G at bonds -Gly!Arg- and -Lys!Arg-
gingipain K. Endopeptidase with strict specificity for lysyl bonds

staphopain. Broad endopeptidase action on proteins including elastin, but rather limited hydrolysis of small-molecule substrates. Assays are conveniently made with hemoglobin, casein or Z-Phe-Arg-NHMec as substrate

separase. All bonds known to be hydrolysed by this endopeptidase have arginine in P1 and an acidic residue in P4. P6 is often occupied by an acidic residue or by an hydroxy-amino-acid residue, the phosphorylation of which enhances cleavage
V-cath endopeptidase. Endopeptidase of broad specificity, hydrolysing substrates of both cathepsin L and cathepsin B
cruzipain. Broad endopeptidase specificity similar to that of cathepsin L
calpain-1. Broad endopeptidase specificity
calpain-2. Broad endopeptidase specificity
calpain-3. Broad endopeptidase activity
caspase-2. Strict requirement for an Asp residue at P1, with Asp316 being essential for proteolytic activity and has a preferred cleavage sequence of Val-Asp-Val-Ala-Asp!

caspase-3. Strict requirement for an Asp residue at positions P1 and P4. It has a preferred cleavage sequence of Asp-Xaa-Xaa-Asp! with a hydrophobic amino-acid residue at P2 and a hydrophilic amino-acid residue at P3, although Val or Ala are also accepted at this position
caspase-4. Strict requirement for Asp at the P1 position. It has a preferred cleavage sequence of Tyr-Val-Ala-Asp! but also cleaves at Asp-Glu-Val-Asp!
caspase-5. Strict requirement for Asp at the P1 position. It has a preferred cleavage sequence of Tyr-Val-Ala-Asp! but also cleaves at Asp-Glu-Val-Asp!
caspase-6. Strict requirement for Asp at position P1 and has a preferred cleavage sequence of Val-Glu-His-Asp!
chymopapain. Similar to that of papain
caspase-7. Strict requirement for an Asp residue at position P1 and has a preferred cleavage sequence of Asp-Glu-Val-Asp!
caspase-8. Strict requirement for Asp at position P1 and has a preferred cleavage sequence of (Leu/Asp/Val)-Glu-Thr-Asp!(Gly/Ser/Ala)
caspase-9. Strict requirement for an Asp residue at position P1 and with a marked preference for His at position P2. It has a preferred cleavage sequence of Leu-Gly-His-Asp!Xaa
caspase-10. Strict requirement for Asp at position P1 and has a preferred cleavage sequence of Leu-Gln-Thr-Asp!Gly
caspase-11. Strict requirement for Asp at the P1 position and has a preferred cleavage sequence of (Ile/Leu/Val/Phe)-Gly-His-Asp!
peptidase 1 (mite). Broad endopeptidase specificity
calicivirin. Endopeptidase with a preference for cleavage when the P1 position is occupied by Glu! and the P1' position is occupied by Gly!
zingipain. Preferential cleavage of peptides with a proline residue at the P2 position

Ulp1 peptidase. Hydrolysis of the alpha-linked peptide bond in the sequence Gly-Gly!Ala-Thr-Tyr at the C-terminal end of the small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) propeptide, Smt3, leading to the mature form of the protein. A second reaction involves the cleavage of an epsilon-linked peptide bond between the C-terminal glycine of the mature SUMO and the lysine epsilon-amino group of the target protein

SARS coronavirus main proteinase. TSAVLQ!SGFRK-NH2 and SGVTFQ!GKFKK the two peptides corresponding to the two self-cleavage sites of the SARS 3C-like proteinase are the two most reactive peptide substrates. The enzyme exhibits a strong preference for substrates containing Gln at P1 position and Leu at P2 position.
asclepain. Similar to that of papain

sortase A. The enzyme catalyses a cell wall sorting reaction in which a surface protein with a sorting signal containing a LPXTG motif is cleaved between the Thr and Gly residue. The resulting threonine carboxyl end of the protein is covalently attached to a pentaglycine cross-bridge of peptidoglycan.

sortase B. The enzyme catalyses a cell wall sorting reaction in which a surface protein with a sorting signal containing a NPXTN motif is cleaved between the Thr and Asn residue. The resulting threonine carboxyl end of the protein is covalently attached to a pentaglycine cross-bridge of peptidoglycan.
clostripain. Preferential cleavage: Arg!, including Arg!Pro, but not Lys-
Aspartic endopeptidases

pepsin A. Preferential cleavage: hydrophobic, preferably aromatic, residues in P1 and P1' positions. Cleaves Phe1!Val, Gln4!His, Glu13!Ala, Ala14!Leu, Leu15!Tyr, Tyr16!Leu, Gly23!Phe, Phe24!Phe and Phe25!Tyr bonds in the B chain of insulin
nepenthesin. Similar to pepsin, but also cleaves on either side of Asp and at Lys!Arg
renin. Cleavage of Leu! bond in angiotensinogen to generate angiotensin I
HIV-1 retropepsin. Specific for a P1 residue that is hydrophobic, and P1' variable, but often Pro
pro-opiomelanocortin converting enzyme. Cleavage at paired basic residues in certain prohormones, either between them, or on the carboxyl side

aspergillopepsin I. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity. Generally favours hydrophobic residues in P1 and P1', but also accepts Lys in P1, which leads to activation of trypsinogen. Does not clot milk
aspergillopepsin II. Preferential cleavage in B chain of insulin: Asn3!Gln, Gly13!Ala, Tyr26!Thr
pepsin B. Degradation of gelatin; little activity on hemoglobin. Specificity on B chain of insulin more restricted than that of pepsin A; does not cleave at Phe1-Val, Gln4-His or Gly23-Phe

penicillopepsin. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity similar to that of pepsin A, preferring hydrophobic residues at P1 and P1', but also cleaving Gly20!Glu in the B chain of insulin. Clots milk, and activates trypsinogen

rhizopuspepsin. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity similar to that of pepsin A, preferring hydrophobic residues at P1 and P1'. Clots milk and activates trypsinogen. Does not cleave Gln4-His, but does cleave His10!Leu and Val12!Glu in B chain of insulin

endothiapepsin. Hydrolysis of proteins with specificity similar to that of pepsin A; prefers hydrophobic residues at P1 and P1', but does not cleave Ala14-Leu in the B chain of insulin or Z-Glu-Tyr. Clots milk
mucorpepsin. Hydrolysis of proteins, favouring hydrophobic residues at P1 and P1'. Clots milk. Does not accept Lys at P1, and hence does not activate trypsinogen
candidapepsin. Preferential cleavage at the carboxyl of hydrophobic amino acids, but fails to cleave Leu15-Tyr, Tyr16-Leu and Phe24-Phe of insulin B chain. Activates trypsinogen, and degrades keratin
saccharopepsin. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity for peptide bonds. Cleaves -Leu-Leu!Val-Tyr bond in a synthetic substrate. Does not act on esters of Tyr or Arg
rhodotorulapepsin. Specificity similar to that of pepsin A. Cleaves Z-Lys!Ala-Ala-Ala and activates trypsinogen

acrocylindropepsin. Preference for hydrophobic residues at P1 and P1'. Action on the B chain of insulin is generally similar to that of pepsin A, but it also cleaves Leu6!Cys(SO3H), Glu21!Arg and Asn3!Gln, although not Gln4-His
polyporopepsin. Milk clotting activity, broad specificity, but fails to cleave Leu15-Tyr or Tyr16-Leu of insulin B chain
gastricsin. More restricted specificity than pepsin A, but shows preferential cleavage at Tyr! bonds. High activity on hemoglobin
pycnoporopepsin. Similar to pepsin A, but narrower, cleaving only three bonds in the B chain of insulin: Ala14!Leu, Tyr16!Leu, and Phe24!Phe
scytalidopepsin A. Hydrolysis of proteins with specificity similar to that of pepsin A, but also cleaves Cys(SO3H)7!Gly and Leu17!Val in the B chain of insulin
scytalidopepsin B. Hydrolysis of proteins with broad specificity, cleaving Phe24!Phe, but not Leu15-Tyr and Phe25-Tyr in the B chain of insulin
cathepsin E. Similar to cathepsin D, but slightly broader specificity
barrierpepsin. Selective cleavage of -Leu6!Lys- bond in the pheromone alpha-mating factor

signal peptidase II. Release of signal peptides from bacterial membrane prolipoproteins including murein prolipoprotein. Hydrolyses -Xaa-Yaa-Zaa!(S,diacylglyceryl)Cys-, in which Xaa is hydrophobic (preferably Leu), and Yaa (Ala or Ser) and Zaa (Gly or Ala) have small, neutral sidechains
plasmepsin I. Hydrolysis of the -Phe33!Leu- bond in the alpha-chain of hemoglobin, leading to denaturation of the molecule

plasmepsin II. Hydrolysis of the bonds linking certain hydrophobic residues in hemoglobin or globin. Also cleaves the small molecule substrates such as Ala-Leu-Glu-Arg-Thr-Phe!Phe(NO2)-Ser-Phe-Pro-Thr [3]
chymosin. Broad specificity similar to that of pepsin A. Clots milk by cleavage of a single Ser-Phe105!Met-Ala bond in kappa-chain of casein
phytepsin. Prefers hydrophobic residues Phe, Val, Ile, Leu, and Ala at P1 and P1', but also cleaves -Phe!Asp- and -Asp!Asp- bonds in 2S albumin from plant seeds

yapsin 1. Hydrolyses various precursor proteins with Arg or Lys in P1, and commonly Arg or Lys also in P2. The P3 amino acid is usually non-polar, but otherwise additional basic amino acids are favourable in both non-prime and prime positions
thermopsin. Similar in specificity to pepsin A preferring bulky hydrophobic amino acids in P1 and P1'

prepilin peptidase. Typically cleaves a -Gly!Phe- bond to release an N-terminal, basic peptide of 5-8 residues from type IV prepilin, and then N-methylates the new N-terminal amino group, the methyl donor being S-adenosyl-L-methionine
nodavirus endopeptidase. Hydrolysis of an asparaginyl bond involved in the maturation of the structural protein of the virus, typically -Asn!Ala- or -Asn!Phe-
memapsin 1. Broad endopeptidase specificity. Cleaves Glu-Val-Asn-Leu!Asp-Ala-Glu-Phe in the Swedish variant of Alzheimer's amyloid precursor protein
memapsin 2. Broad endopeptidase specificity. Cleaves Glu-Val-Asn-Leu!Asp-Ala-Glu-Phe in the Swedish variant of Alzheimer's amyloid precursor protein
HIV-2 retropepsin. Endopeptidase for which the P1 residue is preferably hydrophobic

plasminogen activator Pla. Converts human Glu-plasminogen to plasmin by cleaving the Arg560!Val peptide bond that is also hydrolysed by the mammalian u-plasminogen activator and t-plasminogen activator. Also cleaves arginyl bonds in other proteins
omptin. Has a virtual requirement for Arg in the P1 position and a slightly less stringent preference for this residue in the P1' position, which can also contain Lys, Gly or Val.
cathepsin D. Specificity similar to, but narrower than, that of pepsin A. Does not cleave the Gln4-His bond in B chain of insulin

human endogenous retrovirus K endopeptidase. Processing at the authentic HIV-1 PR recognition site and release of the mature p17 matrix and the p24 capsid protein, as a result of the cleavage of the -SQNY!PIVQ- cleavage site.

HycI peptidase. This enzyme specifically removes a 32-amino acid peptide from the C-terminus of the precursor of the large subunit of hydrogenase 3 in Escherichia coli by cleavage at the C-terminal side of Arg537.
preflagellin peptidase. Cleaves the signal peptide of 3 to 12 amino acids from the N-terminal of preflagellin, usually at Arg-Gly! or Lys-Gly!, to release flagellin.
Metalloendopeptidases
atrolysin A. Cleavage of Asn3!Gln, His5!Leu, His10!Leu, Ala14!Leu and Tyr16!Leu in insulin B chain; removes C-terminal Leu from small peptides
neprilysin. Preferential cleavage of polypeptides between hydrophobic residues, particularly with Phe or Tyr at P1'
envelysin. Hydrolysis of proteins of the fertilization envelope and dimethylcasein
IgA-specific metalloendopeptidase. Cleavage of Pro!Thr bond in the hinge region of the heavy chain of human IgA
procollagen N-endopeptidase. Cleaves the N-propeptide of collagen chain alpha1(I) at Pro!Gln and of alpha1(II) and alpha2(I) at Ala!Gln
thimet oligopeptidase. Preferential cleavage of bonds with hydrophobic residues at P1, P2 and P3' and a small residue at P1' in substrates of 5-15 residues
neurolysin. Preferential cleavage in neurotensin: Pro10!Tyr
stromelysin 1. Preferential cleavage where P1', P2' and P3' are hydrophobic residues
meprin A. Hydrolysis of protein and peptide substrates preferentially on carboxyl side of hydrophobic residues
procollagen C-endopeptidase. Cleavage of the C-terminal propeptide at Ala!Asp in type I and II procollagens and at Arg!Asp in type III
peptidyl-Lys metalloendopeptidase. Preferential cleavage in proteins: -Xaa!Lys- (in which Xaa may be Pro)
astacin. Hydrolysis of peptide bonds in substrates containing five or more amino acids, preferentially with Ala in P1', and Pro in P2'
stromelysin 2. Similar to stromelysin 1, but action on collagen types III, IV and V is weak
matrilysin. Cleavage of Ala14!Leu and Tyr16!Leu in B chain of insulin. No action on collagen types I, II, IV, V. Cleaves gelatin chain alpha2(I) > alpha1(I)
gelatinase A. Cleavage of gelatin type I and collagen types IV, V, VII, X. Cleaves the collagen-like sequence Pro-Gln-Gly!Ile-Ala-Gly-Gln
vibriolysin. Preferential cleavage of bonds with bulky hydrophobic groups in P2 and P1'. Phe at P1' is the most favoured residue, which distinguished this enzyme from thermolysin

pseudolysin. Hydrolysis of proteins including elastin, collagen types III and IV, fibronectin and immunoglobulin A, generally with bulky hydrophobic group at P1'. Insulin B chain cleavage pattern identical to that of thermolysin, but specificity differs in other respects
thermolysin. Preferential cleavage: !Leu > !Phe
bacillolysin. Similar, but not identical, to that of thermolysin

aureolysin. Cleavage of insulin B chain with specificity similar to that of thermolysin, preferring hydrophobic P1' residue. Activates the glutamyl endopeptidase (EC 3.4.21.19) of Staphylococcus aureus

microbial collagenase. Digestion of native collagen in the triple helical region at !Gly bonds. With synthetic peptides, a preference is shown for Gly at P3 and P1', Pro and Ala at P2 and P2', and hydroxyproline, Ala or Arg at P3'
coccolysin. Preferential cleavage: !Leu, !Phe, !Tyr, !Ala
mycolysin. Preferential cleavage of bonds with hydrophobic residues in P1'
beta-lytic metalloendopeptidase. Cleavage of N-acetylmuramoyl!Ala, and of the insulin B chain at Gly23!Phe > Val18!Cya
peptidyl-Asp metalloendopeptidase. Cleavage of Xaa!Asp, Xaa!Glu and Xaa!cysteic acid bonds
neutrophil collagenase. Cleavage of interstitial collagens in the triple helical domain. Unlike EC 3.4.24.7, interstitial collagenase, this enzyme cleaves type III collagen more slowly than type I
gelatinase B. Cleavage of gelatin types I and V and collagen types IV and V
leishmanolysin. Preference for hydrophobic residues at P1 and P1' and basic residues at P2' and P3'. A model nonapeptide is cleaved at -Ala-Tyr!Leu-Lys-Lys-
saccharolysin. Cleavage of Pro!Phe and Ala!Ala bonds
gametolysin. Cleavage of the proline- and hydroxyproline-rich proteins of the Chlamydomonas cell wall; also cleaves azocasein, gelatin and Leu-Trp-Met!Arg-Phe-Ala
deuterolysin. Preferential cleavage of bonds with hydrophobic residues in P1', also Asn3!Gln and Gly8!Ser bonds in insulin B chain
serralysin. Preferential cleavage of bonds with hydrophobic residues in P1'
atrolysin B. Cleavage of His5!Leu, His10!Leu, Ala14!Leu, Tyr16!Leu and Gly23!Phe of insulin B chain; identical to the cleavage of insulin B chain by atrolysin C. Also cleaves !Ser bonds in glucagon

atrolysin C. Cleavage of His5!Leu, His10!Leu, Ala14!Leu, Tyr16!Leu and Gly23!Phe bonds in B chain of insulin. With small molecule substrates prefers hydrophobic residue at P2' and small residue such as Ala, Gly at P1
atroxase. Cleavage of His5!Leu, Ser9!His, His10!Leu, Ala14!Leu and Tyr16!Leu of insulin B chain

atrolysin E. Cleavage of Asn3!Gln, Ser9!His and Ala14!Leu bonds in insulin B chain and Tyr14!Gln and Thr8!Ser in A chain. Cleaves type IV collagen at Ala73!Gln in alpha1(IV) and at Gly7!Leu in alpha2(IV)
atrolysin F. Cleavage of Val2!Asn, Gln4!His, Leu6!Cys, His10!Leu, Ala14!Leu and Tyr16!Leu bonds in insulin B chain
adamalysin. Cleavage of Phe1!Val, His5!Leu, His10!Leu, Ala14!Leu, Leu15!Tyr, and Tyr16!Leu of insulin B chain

mitochondrial intermediate peptidase. Release of an N-terminal octapeptide as second stage of processing of some proteins imported into the mitochondrion
leucolysin. Cleavage of Phe1!Val, His5!Leu, Ala14!Leu, Gly20!Glu, Gly23!Phe and Phe24!Phe bonds in insulin B chain as well as N-blocked dipeptides

dactylysin. Hydrolysis of peptides of at least six residues, with bulky hydrophobic residues in the P1' position. Shows a preference for hydrophobic doublets such as -Phe!Phe- and -Phe!Leu- in somatostatin-(1-14)-peptide and dynorphin A-(1-6)-peptide, respectively
nardilysin. Hydrolysis of polypeptides, preferably at -Xaa!Arg-Lys-, and less commonly at -Arg!Arg-Xaa-, in which Xaa is not Arg or Lys

magnolysin. Hydrolysis of polypeptides with Arg or Lys in P1 and P2, e.g. to hydrolyse pro-oxytocin at -Lys-Arg!Ala-Val-. The specificity further depends on the organization of a beta-turn-alpha-helix of nine or more residues containing the paired basic amino acids near the centre [3]
meprin B. Hydrolysis of proteins, including azocasein, and peptides. Hydrolysis of -His5!Leu-, -Leu6!Cys-, -Ala14!Leu- and -Cys19!Gly- bonds in insulin B chain
mitochondrial processing peptidase. Release of N-terminal targetting peptides from precursor proteins imported into the mitochondrion, typically with Arg in position P2
macrophage elastase. Hydrolysis of soluble and insoluble elastin [1]. Specific cleavages are also produced at -Ala14!Leu- and -Tyr16!Leu- in the B chain of insulin [2]
choriolysin L. Hydrolysis of the inner layer of fish egg envelope. Also hydrolysis of casein and small molecule substrates such as succinyl-Leu-Leu-Val-Tyr!7-(4-methyl)coumarylamide
choriolysin H. Hydrolysis of the inner layer of fish egg envelope. Also hydrolysis of casein and small molecule substrates such as succinyl-Leu-Leu-Val-Tyr!7-(4-methyl)coumarylamide
tentoxilysin. Hydrolysis of -Gln76!Phe- bond in synaptobrevin (also known as neuronal vesicle-associated membrane protein, VAMP)

bontoxilysin. Limited hydrolysis of proteins of the neuroexocytosis apparatus, synaptobrevin (also known as neuronal vesicle-associated membrane protein, VAMP), synaptosome-associated protein of 25 kDa (SNAP25) or syntaxin. No detected action on small molecule substrates

interstitial collagenase. Cleavage of the triple helix of collagen at about three-quarters of the length of the molecule from the N-terminus, at Gly775!Ile in the alpha1(I) chain. Cleaves synthetic substrates and alpha-macroglobulins at bonds where P1' is a hydrophobic residue

oligopeptidase A. Hydrolysis of oligopeptides, with broad specificity. Gly or Ala commonly occur as P1 or P1' residues, but more distant residues are also important, as is shown by the fact that Z-Gly-Pro-Gly!Gly-Pro-Ala is cleaved, but not Z-(Gly)5 [4]

fragilysin. Broad proteolytic specificity, bonds hydrolysed including -Gly!Leu-, -Met!Leu-, -Phe!Leu-, -Cys!Leu-, Leu!Gly
lysostaphin. Hydrolysis of the -Gly!Gly- bond in the pentaglycine inter-peptide link joining staphylococcal cell wall peptidoglycans
flavastacin. Hydrolyses polypeptides on the amino-side of Asp in -Xaa!Asp-. Acts very slowly on -Xaa!Glu

gpr endopeptidase. Endopeptidase action with P4 Glu or Asp, P1 preferably Glu Asp, P1' hydrophobic and P2' Ala

ADAM10 endopeptidase. Endopeptidase of broad specificity
ADAMTS-4 endopeptidase. Glutamyl endopeptidase; bonds cleaved include -Thr-Glu-Gly-Glu373!Ala-Arg-Gly-Ser- in the interglobular domain of mammalian aggrecan

anthrax lethal factor endopeptidase. Preferred amino acids around the cleavage site can be denoted BBBBxHx!H, in which B denotes Arg or Lys, H denotes a hydrophobic amino acid, and x is any amino acid. The only known protein substrates are mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase kinases
Ste24 endopeptidase. Hydrolyses the peptide bond -P2-(S-farnesyl or geranylgeranyl)C-P1'-P2'-P3'-COOH where P1' and P2' are amino acids with aliphatic side chains and P3' is any C-terminal residue.

S2P endopeptidase. Cleaves several transcription factors that are type-2 transmembrane proteins within membrane-spanning domains. Known substrates include sterol regulatory element-binding protein (SREBP) -1, SREBP-2 and forms of the transcriptional activator ATF6. SREBP-2 is cleaved at the site DRSRILL483!CVLTFLCLSFNPLTSLLQWGGA, in which the membrane-spanning segment is underlined. The residues NP (bold), 11 residues distal to the site of cleavage in the membrane-spanning domain, are important for cleavage by S2P endopeptidase. Replacement of either of these residues does not prevent cleavage, but there is no cleavage if both of these residues are replaced.

ADAM 17 endopeptidase. Narrow endopeptidase specificity. Cleaves Pro-Leu-Ala-Gln-Ala!Val-Arg-Ser-Ser-Ser in the membrane-bound, 26-kDa form of tumour necrosis factor alpha (TNFalpha). Similarly cleaves other membrane-anchored, cell-surface proteins to "shed" the extracellular domains
ADAMTS13 endopeptidase. The enzyme cleaves the von Willebrand factor at bond Tyr842!Met843 within the A2 domain

Acting on polysaccharides
hyaluronate lyase. Cleaves hyaluronate chains at a beta-D-GlcNAc-(1->4)-beta-D-GlcA bond, ultimately breaking the polysaccharide down to 3-(4-deoxy-beta-D-gluc-4-enuronosyl)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine.
pectin lyase. Eliminative cleavage of (1->4)-alpha-D-galacturonan methyl ester to give oligosaccharides with 4-deoxy-6-O-methyl-alpha-D-galact-4-enuronosyl groups at their non-reducing ends

guluronate-specific alginate lyase. Eliminative cleavage of alginate to give oligosaccharides with 4-deoxy-alpha-L-erythro-hex-4-enuronosyl groups at their non-reducing ends and alpha-L-guluronate at their reducing end.

xanthan lyase. Eliminative cleavage of the terminal beta-D-mannosyl-(1->4)-beta-D-glucuronosyl linkage of the side-chain of the polysaccharide xanthan, leaving a 4-deoxy-alpha-L-threo-hex-4-enuronosyl group at the terminus of the side-chain
exo-(1->4)-alpha-D-glucan lyase. linear alpha-glucan = (n-1) 1,5-anhydro-D-fructose + D-glucose

glucuronan lyase. Eliminative cleavage of (1->4)-beta-D-glucuronans to give oligosaccharides with 4-deoxy-beta-D-gluc-4-enuronosyl groups at their non-reducing ends. Complete degradation of glucuronans results in the formation of tetrasaccharides.
anhydrosialidase. Elimination of alpha-sialyl groups in N-acetylneuraminic acid glycosides, releasing 2,7-anhydro-alpha-N-acetylneuraminate

levan fructotransferase (DFA-IV-forming). Produces di-beta-D-fructofuranose 2,6':2',6-dianhydride (DFA IV) by successively eliminating the diminishing (2->6)-beta-D-fructan (levan) chain from the terminal D-fructosyl-D-fructosyl disaccharide

inulin fructotransferase (DFA-I-forming). Produces alpha-D-fructofuranose beta-D-fructofuranose 1,2':2,1'-dianhydride (DFA I) by successively eliminating the diminishing (2->1)-beta-D-fructan (inulin) chain from the terminal D-fructosyl-D-fructosyl disaccharide.

inulin fructotransferase (DFA-III-forming). Produces alpha-D-fructofuranose beta-D-fructofuranose 1,2':2,3'-dianhydride (DFA III) by successively eliminating the diminishing (2->1)-beta-D-fructan (inulin) chain from the terminal D-fructosyl-D-fructosyl disaccharide.

chondroitin B lyase. Eliminative cleavage of dermatan sulfate containing (1->4)-beta-D-hexosaminyl and (1->3)-beta-D-glucurosonyl or (1->3)-alpha-L-iduronosyl linkages to disaccharides containing 4-deoxy-beta-D-gluc-4-enuronosyl groups to yield a 4,5-unsaturated dermatan-sulfate disaccharide (DeltaUA-GalNAc-4S).
pectate lyase. Eliminative cleavage of (1->4)-alpha-D-galacturonan to give oligosaccharides with 4-deoxy-alpha-D-galact-4-enuronosyl groups at their non-reducing ends

chondroitin-sulfate-ABC endolyase. Endolytic cleavage of (1->4)-beta-galactosaminic bonds between N-acetylgalactosamine and either D-glucuronic acid or L-iduronic acid to produce a mixture of Delta4-unsaturated oligosaccharides of different sizes that are ultimately degraded to Delta4-unsaturated tetra- and disaccharides

chondroitin-sulfate-ABC exolyase. Exolytic removal of Delta4-unsaturated disaccharide residues from the non-reducing ends of both polymeric chondroitin/dermatan sulfates and their oligosaccharide fragments.
pectate trisaccharide-lyase. eliminative cleavage of unsaturated trigalacturonate as the major product from the reducing end of polygalacturonic acid/pectate

rhamnogalacturonan endolyase. Endotype eliminative cleavage of L-alpha-rhamnopyranosyl-(1->4)-alpha-D-galactopyranosyluronic acid bonds of rhamnogalacturonan I domains in ramified hairy regions of pectin leaving L-rhamnopyranose at the reducing end and 4-deoxy-4,5-unsaturated D-galactopyranosyluronic acid at the non-reducing end.

rhamnogalacturonan exolyase. Exotype eliminative cleavage of alpha-L-rhamnopyranosyl-(1->4)-alpha-D-galactopyranosyluronic acid bonds of rhamnogalacturonan I oligosaccharides containing alpha-L-rhamnopyranose at the reducing end and 4-deoxy-4,5-unsaturated D-galactopyranosyluronic acid at the non-reducing end. The products are the disaccharide 2-O-(4-deoxy-beta-L-threo-hex-4-enopyranuronosyl)-alpha-L-rhamnopyranose and the shortened rhamnogalacturonan oligosaccharide containing one 4-deoxy-4,5-unsaturated D-galactopyranosyluronic acid at the non-reducing end.

gellan lyase. Eliminative cleavage of beta-D-glucopyranosyl-(1->4)-beta-D-glucopyranosyluronate bonds of gellan backbone releasing tetrasaccharides containing a 4-deoxy-4,5-unsaturated D-glucopyranosyluronic acid at the non-reducing end. The tetrasaccharide produced from deacetylated gellan is beta-D-4-deoxy-Delta4-GlcAp-(1->4)-beta-D-Glcp-(1->4)-alpha-L-Rhap-(1->3)-beta-D-Glcp.

oligo-alginate lyase. Cleavage of poly(4-deoxy-alpha-L-erythro-hexopyranuronoside) oligosaccharides with 4-deoxy-alpha-L-erythro-hex-4-enopyranuronosyl groups at their non-reducing ends into 4-deoxy-alpha-L-erythro-hex-4-enopyranuronate monosaccharides.
pectin monosaccharide-lyase. (1,4-alpha-D-galacturonosyl methyl ester)n = (1,4-alpha-D-galacturonosyl methyl ester)n-1 + 4-deoxy-6-O-methyl-L-threo-hex-4-enopyranuronate
alpha-L-rhamnosyl-(1->4)-D-glucuronate lyase. alpha-L-rhamnosyl-(1->4)-D-glucuronate = L-rhamnopyranose + 4-deoxy-L-threo-hex-4-enopyranuronate

peptidoglycan lytic transglycosylase. a peptidoglycan chain = a peptidoglycan chain with N-acetyl-1,6-anhydromuramyl-(peptide) at the reducing end + a peptidoglycan chain with N-acetylglucosamine at the non-reducing end

mannuronate-specific alginate lyase. Eliminative cleavage of alginate to give oligosaccharides with 4-deoxy-alpha-L-erythro-hex-4-enuronosyl groups at their non-reducing ends and beta-D-mannuronate at their reducing end.

chondroitin ABC lyase. Eliminative degradation of polysaccharides containing 1,4-beta-D-hexosaminyl and 1,3-beta-D-glucuronosyl or 1,3-alpha-L-iduronosyl linkages to disaccharides containing 4-deoxy-beta-D-gluc-4-enuronosyl groups

chondroitin AC lyase. Eliminative degradation of polysaccharides containing 1,4-beta-D-hexosaminyl and 1,3-beta-D-glucuronosyl linkages to disaccharides containing 4-deoxy-beta-D-gluc-4-enuronosyl groups
oligogalacturonide lyase. 4-(4-deoxy-alpha-D-galact-4-enuronosyl)-D-galacturonate = 2 5-dehydro-4-deoxy-D-glucuronate

heparin lyase. Eliminative cleavage of polysaccharides containing (1->4)-linked D-glucuronate or L-iduronate residues and (1->4)-alpha-linked 2-sulfoamino-2-deoxy-6-sulfo-D-glucose residues to give oligosaccharides with terminal 4-deoxy-alpha-D-gluc-4-enuronosyl groups at their non-reducing ends
heparin-sulfate lyase. Elimination of sulfate; appears to act on linkages between N-acetyl-D-glucosamine and uronate. Product is an unsaturated sugar.
pectate disaccharide-lyase. (1,4-alpha-D-galacturonosyl)n = (1,4-alpha-D-galacturonosyl)n-2 + 4-(4-deoxy-alpha-D-galact-4-enuronosyl)-D-galacturonate
